passage: Hot take after six years of coaching: there are two kinds of gym-goers. Either you commit to heavy barbell work, or you accept staying exactly where you are. Cardio machines and light dumbbells are fine for warming up, but that's about it. Who's starting a real program Monday?
cue: Either you commit to heavy barbell work, or you accept staying exactly where you are
explanation: Dani allows only two paths, heavy barbell work or no progress at all, skipping bodyweight training, machines, classes, sport, or a mix of approaches.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: Dani isn't claiming a compromise is right; the problem is that only two options are allowed to exist.

passage:
Marisol: QA found two bugs in checkout. Small, but customers will definitely hit them.
Kofi: Then we have a choice. We ship Thursday as announced, or we tell the whole company this team can't deliver.
Ines: How long would the fixes actually take?
cue: We ship Thursday as announced, or we tell the whole company this team can't deliver
explanation: Kofi frames it as ship on schedule or admit failure, ignoring a short delay, a phased release, or shipping with checkout turned off until it's fixed.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: Kofi isn't asking a question with a built-in assumption; he's presenting a choice with too few options.

title: Re: Grade 7 math placement
passage: Hi Ms. Adeyemi, thanks for the detailed placement report. I agree Noor's quiz scores dropped this term, and I appreciate you flagging it early. That said, I don't want her moved. As I see it, she stays in accelerated math, or she decides she's 'not a math person' for good. We'd like to keep her where she is. Best, Hana
cue: she stays in accelerated math, or she decides she's 'not a math person' for good
explanation: Hana reduces the decision to two outcomes, staying accelerated or giving up on math forever, leaving out tutoring, a temporary move with a review date, or extra support.

whyNot.fal_slippery_slope: Hana doesn't describe a chain of steps leading somewhere bad; she presents just two possible outcomes as if nothing else could happen.

source: Councillor Rina Castellanos · Millcaster council meeting
passage: Thank you all for coming out tonight. The Harlow Street pool is sixty years old, and the engineers' report confirms the filtration system is failing. I won't pretend that's cheap to fix. But let's be honest about what's in front of us: we approve the full $4 million rebuild this spring, or Millcaster kids spend their summers without a pool.
cue: we approve the full $4 million rebuild this spring, or Millcaster kids spend their summers without a pool
explanation: Rina's report shows a real problem, but she skips everything between a full rebuild and no pool, such as replacing just the filtration system or rebuilding in phases.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: Rina isn't saying the halfway option is right; she's hiding the fact that halfway options exist at all.

title: Quiet and long-lasting, but I sent it back
passage: Battery life is great and it's quiet enough to run during video calls. The issue is navigation. Robot vacuums come in two kinds: lidar models that map your home, and cheap ones that bounce around at random. There's no lidar turret on this one, so you can guess which camp it's in. Mine went back after a week.
cue: come in two kinds: lidar models that map your home, and cheap ones that bounce around at random
explanation: Tobias sorts every robot vacuum into lidar mapping or random bouncing, overlooking camera- and sensor-based models that clean in planned rows without a lidar turret.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: Tobias isn't generalizing from a few cases; he starts from a two-category split that leaves out other ways of navigating.

title: Hospital board weighs $9M ER expansion as visits climb 18%
passage: Board chair Wen Moreau told Tuesday's meeting that Larkwell General's emergency department saw 18% more visits this year than last. "The math is simple," she said. "We find $9 million to expand the ER, or residents accept waits that keep getting longer." A vote is expected in March.
cue: We find $9 million to expand the ER, or residents accept waits that keep getting longer
explanation: The rise in visits is real, but Wen treats expansion as the only fix for waits, leaving out options like an urgent-care clinic for minor cases, more night staff, or better triage.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: Wen isn't pushing a compromise as automatically right; she leaves out the alternative fixes entirely.

title: Garden grant deadline
passage: Hi all, quick update on the city garden grant. The application portal closes this Friday at 5 p.m., and it only opens once a year. So our real options are to submit by Friday or wait until next fall. Waiting would cost us the spring planting season, and the draft is nearly done, so I think we should finish it Thursday night. Amara
cue: it only opens once a year
explanation: Amara's two options really are the only ones: the portal opens once a year, so it's submit by Friday or wait a year. She then gives a reason to prefer submitting.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: The two choices are exhaustive because of a stated fact, a single yearly window, not because other options were ignored.

passage:
Coach Tamsin: Reminder: Saturday's semifinal is single elimination. Win and we play the final on the 14th; lose and the season's over.
Rafael: What if it ends in a draw?
Coach Tamsin: Draws go straight to penalty kicks, so there's no third result. Please keep the 14th free just in case.
cue: Draws go straight to penalty kicks, so there's no third result
explanation: Tamsin's either/or is genuine: in a knockout game decided by penalty kicks, every match ends in a win or a loss, so planning around both outcomes makes sense.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: Tamsin checks the possible third outcome, a draw, and shows the rules rule it out, so the two options really are exhaustive.
